blocks.html:
Welcome to the official SlideCast Studio manual.

SlideCast Studio is a slide-video tool I built by heavily modifying an idea I found in a note post by Majin. It only exists because Majin published the prompt in the first place.

items.title: [Free] The "prompt" that turns NotebookLM slides into a video with audio and subtitles

blocks.html: I took that prompt, modified it heavily, and turned it into an Apps Script app: SlideCast Studio v1.0.

items.title: [Amazing tool] A follower's "heavily modified" tool is too good [SlideCast Studio]

blocks.html: SlideCast Studio v2 and later — what this manual covers — is a large update on top of that.

blocks.title: 🌐 About the screenshots and labels
blocks.text: The screenshots on this page show the Japanese interface. The app itself also runs in English (switch with the language button at the bottom of the left-hand icon rail), and this manual uses the English labels. In English, the rail reads Slides, Script, This slide and Project.

blocks.title: 🧭 How to read this manual
blocks.text: If this is your first time, the shortest path is chapter 4, “The dashboard and how to start a project”. If you used v5.0 or earlier, the layout has changed, so read chapter 5, “A map of the editor”, first. Click any chapter heading to open it.

blocks.title: 🎬 Prefer video?
blocks.text: The tutorial videos, re-recorded on the v5.5 screens, are lined up chapter by chapter on the video manual page. Each chapter here also ends with links to the matching videos. The videos are narrated and captioned in Japanese.

sections.title: Introduction and main features

blocks.html: SlideCast Studio loads PDFs, images and videos into your browser, adds narration, captions, characters and background music, and exports the result straight to video. Nothing to install: all the work happens inside your own browser.

items.title: Bundle Builder
items.text: A companion tool that makes the script and voice from your material in one pass, with no API key to set up

items.title: Start from a use
items.text: Build a project by picking the aspect ratio, a screen layout, characters and a caption design

items.title: Preview to settings
items.text: Click what you want to change in the preview and jump to its setting

items.title: 32 caption designs
items.text: Bands, outlines, shadows and more. 22 motions, emphasis, karaoke and name badges

items.title: Character acting
items.text: Lip sync, speaking motion, expressions, gestures and auto acting

items.title: Stickers, tickers and badges
items.text: Stick text or images on, scroll them across, or pin them to a corner. With emphasis, tilt and motion

items.title: Video slides
items.text: Drop in MP4 or WebM as a slide and set its sound and the range to play

items.title: BGM (up to 10 tracks)
items.text: Switch tracks from a given slide and crossfade between them

items.title: Timeline
items.text: Fine-tune where each line starts, the gaps and the slide length, to the second

items.title: OP / ED
items.text: Put an opening and an ending video before and after

items.title: Export
items.text: Video (MP4, WebM), PPTX, PDF, book-style PDF and image ZIPs

items.label: 🌐 Display language
items.value: Japanese and English (switch with the button on the left-hand icon rail)

items.label: 💾 Export formats
items.value: MP4, WebM, PPTX, PDF, PNG, JPEG

sections.intro: What SlideCast Studio is and what it can do.

sections.title: System requirements and recommended specs

blocks.html: 🌐 Recommended browsers

items: ✅ Google Chrome (desktop, current version) ← the top recommendation
✅ Microsoft Edge (current version)
⚠️ Phones and tablets are not recommended

blocks.html:
💻 How many slides you can expect to handle

Rendering the video uses your own computer's browser memory.

There are three output resolutions: 720p, 1080p and 1440p (at 16:9 that is 1280×720, 1920×1080 and 2560×1440).

Other recommended specs

items.label: OS
items.value: Windows 11 or later, or macOS 13 or later

items.label: CPU
items.value: 6 cores or more recommended

items.label: Storage
items.value: SSD recommended

blocks.html: 🐢 If things feel slow

items: Drop the output resolution from 1440p to 1080p or below
Drop the video quality from High to Standard or Low
Lower the import quality and import again (chapter 4)
Clear out projects and assets you no longer need
Restart the browser
Split long jobs into several projects

blocks.title: 🫨 If the exported video stutters
blocks.text: The Standard (recording) export method records while it plays, so it depends on spare memory and processing power in the browser. Pause other work and close spare tabs while it exports, and the video comes out smoother. Choose High quality (frame rendering) as the export method and dropped frames and audio drift caused by load cannot happen (chapter 13).

sections.intro: Video export runs on your own computer. Here is what to aim for if you want it to be comfortable.

sections.title: Data storage and security

blocks.html:
💾 Where is everything saved?

All project data is saved “inside your browser (IndexedDB)”. Nothing is uploaded to an outside server.

⚠️ When data can disappear

items: When you clear the browser's “browsing history and cookies”
When you uninstall the browser
When you close an incognito (private) window

blocks.title: 🆘 It cannot be recovered
blocks.text: Once data is gone, the app cannot bring it back. Regular backups are the only protection.

blocks.html: 🔐 If you use an API key

items: Never enter it on a shared computer or in an internet café
The API key is not saved in your project data. It is stored only in the browser
The default storage duration is This session (recommended): the key disappears when you close the tab or browser. Choose This device to keep using it the next time you start the app
For peace of mind, set a monthly spending cap per project on the “Spend” page of Google AI Studio

blocks.title: ⚠️ Leak risk
blocks.text: If an API key ever leaks and is misused, it can lead to a large bill.

blocks.title: 🔒 Privacy & Safety in the app
blocks.text: When the app talks to outside services, where your data stays and how to cap API charges are summarised under Help on the left-hand icon rail → the Privacy & Safety tab.

blocks.text: 🧩 Make the script and voice in Bundle Builder first

blocks.html: Bundle Builder is a companion tool that takes you as far as the script and the voice without any API key. On the dashboard, open Bundle Builder and press “Open in Gemini Canvas” to start it in your browser.

items.title: Material
items.text: Bring in PDFs or images as your material, or have AI create slide images

items.title: Script
items.text: Choose the audience, the length and the cast (with or without a narrator, how many characters), then generate the script. You can also write it yourself or import a script JSON from another AI

items.title: Voice
items.text: Pick a voice for each speaker, listen to a sample, then generate them all. You see a cost estimate first (models used inside Canvas cost nothing)

items.title: Validate
items.text: Empty script fields and the link between speakers and voices are checked automatically

items.title: Export the ZIP
items.text: Download a finished Bundle ZIP containing the slides, script and voice

blocks.text: 🎯 Start from a use (from a finished Bundle ZIP)

blocks.html: You go through four steps shown across the top: Screen, Files, Characters and Design. The preview on the right shows what the project will look like with your choices.

blocks.alt: The Screen step of Start from a use: the aspect ratios and a grid of horizontal and vertical screen types
blocks.caption: The Screen step: choose the aspect ratio and type

items.title: Screen
items.text: Choose the Aspect ratio (16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:5, 4:3) and a Type. In the grid of types, the rows are how characters appear (captions only, character with speech bubbles, wipe and so on) and the columns are where captions go (Below, separate / Over, bottom, middle or top). Hover over one to compare it in the preview. Recommended underneath sets the caption size and similar options in one go

items.title: Files
items.text: Add a finished Bundle ZIP with Select files, check the import quality and press Start import with this quality. The voice in the ZIP is used as is

items.title: Characters
items.text: For each speaker in the script, choose the character shown on screen. Sample placeholder characters are set at first. + Add a new character takes a MouthLoop character pack ZIP or character images. Narration (no character) gives captions with no icon

items.title: Design
items.text: Choose a caption design on the Narration tab and a speech-bubble design on each character's tab, then press Create to open the editor

blocks.alt: The Characters step of Start from a use: choosing a character for each speaker and checking it in the preview
blocks.caption: The Characters step: choose a character for each speaker

blocks.title: 💡 You can change it all later
blocks.text: The aspect ratio, type and design can be changed after the project is created, under Project. Characters you add are saved to the character list and can be used in other projects too.

blocks.html:
Create from files turns the PDFs or images you have straight into slides. There are two ways in, Select files and Select folder. Each PDF page and each image becomes one slide (images inside a ZIP go in filename order). Export PowerPoint and similar decks to PDF first, then import them.

Blank project opens the editor with no slides. Add material from Add slide on the left, or make an empty slide with Add blank slide.
When you import material, you choose how detailed the images used in the video should be. The default is Full HD (up to 1920 pixels on the long side), which is enough for a video headed to YouTube.

items.label: Original quality
items.value: Imports at high quality, capped at the original image (PDFs in high definition)

items.label: 4K
items.value: For 4K video material. Uses more time and memory

items.label: 2K
items.value: A balance of quality and speed

items.label: Full HD (default)
items.value: For standard YouTube use

items.label: Standard
items.value: For everyday use. A little lighter

items.label: Fast
items.value: For checking. Fine text tends to soften

blocks.alt: The import quality chooser
blocks.caption: Choosing the import quality

blocks.title: ⚠️ The source is the ceiling
blocks.text: Choosing a higher quality never makes the result sharper than the original material.

items.title: #01 Make the script and voice in Bundle Builder
#02 Start from a use with a finished Bundle
#03 Start from files, images or a blank slide

blocks.html: Your projects appear as cards on the dashboard. Each card shows a rough measure of its actual data and its backup size.

items: 📋 Duplicate
✏️ Rename
☁️ Save backup (just that project, as a ZIP)

blocks.html: The top of the dashboard shows how much browser storage is in use (an estimate). As it nears the limit, delete projects you no longer need, or back them up and move them out.

sections.intro: Starting from Bundle Builder is recommended. You can also start from your own files or a blank project.

blocks.alt: The whole editor: the icon rail on the far left, the script sidebar, the preview in the middle and the playback bar under it
blocks.caption: The whole editor (with Script open)

items.label: Header (top)
items.value: Back to the dashboard, the project name, Script (generate or import a script), the estimated running time and size, undo / redo, Full preview, Export slides, Export video, and the save status

items.label: Icon rail (far left)
items.value: From the top: Slides, Script, This slide and Project. Click one and its contents appear in the sidebar right next to it. Click the open one again to close the sidebar. At the bottom are the language switch and Help

items.value: Timeline (clock) and BGM (music note) buttons at the top left; the preview background (light, medium, dark) at the top right

blocks.title: ℹ️ What is different from v5.0
blocks.text: The script and timeline panel at the bottom is gone: the script moved to Script on the left, and the timeline to the clock button at the top left of the preview. The settings button moved from the header to Project on the icon rail. Clicking the preview no longer plays or pauses; play from the button in the playback bar. The settings search box, the timing adjustment mode and the easy mode have been removed.

blocks.html: Settings are split in two by how far they reach.

items.label: This slide
items.value: Adjustments for the current slide only. Tabs: Still image display (Video playback on a video slide), Placement, Stickers and Auto acting. With the arrows and the numbered list at the top you can step through the slides and fine-tune them one by one

items.label: Project
items.value: Settings that apply to every slide. Tabs: Screen, Captions, Effects, BGM, OP/ED, Badges, Tickers, Characters and Audio

items.alt: The strip at the top of This slide
items.caption: This slide (この1枚): other slides stay as they are

items.alt: The strip at the top of Project
items.caption: Project (全体設定): applies to every slide

blocks.html: Settings save automatically and show up in the preview right away (only character edits wait for Save shared character). While settings are open, undo with the arrow at the bottom or Ctrl / ⌘ + Z.

blocks.text: 🔦 From the preview to the setting

blocks.html: When you do not know where a setting lives, follow it from the preview. Hover over the paused preview and the frontmost item (caption, character, name badge, sticker, badge, ticker, slide image or background) is outlined with a dashed frame and a name tag. Click it and the Adjust this menu opens.

items.alt: The Adjust this menu after clicking a caption
items.caption: The Adjust this (ここを調整する) menu

items.alt: After clicking Outline, the caption design editor opens on its outline tab
items.caption: The item you land on flashes

items: Each row starts with where it leads: This slide or Project
The buttons under each row go straight to the items inside (for a caption: design, font, outline, karaoke and so on)
Background music does not appear on screen, so reach its setting from the music note at the top left of the preview
Close the menu by clicking outside it or pressing Esc. It does not open when you have just dragged something
The guide works while the slide list or script is showing, or with the sidebar closed (not while This slide or Project is open)
Play just the current slide: the play button in the playback bar, or Space
Play the whole thing: Full preview in the header. It runs with transitions, OP/ED and BGM. Press End to go back to editing

sections.intro: The layout changed a lot in v5.5. Start by getting a feel for where everything is.

sections.title: Slides, script and voice

blocks.html: Open the list with Slides on the left. Click a thumbnail to go to that slide and drag to reorder. Add slide at the very bottom adds material from files or a folder, and Add blank slide adds an empty slide. You can also drop images, videos, PDFs or ZIPs onto the list.

blocks.alt: The slide list, with transition tags between the thumbnails
blocks.caption: The slide list

items: Hover over a thumbnail for actions such as changing the image, duplicating and deleting (undo a delete with Ctrl / ⌘ + Z)
Click the mark for slide-specific settings, or the sticker count, to open the matching tab in This slide
The tag between two slides is the screen transition. Click it to change the setting for just that boundary (chapter 8)
Once you add an OP or ED, rows for them appear at the very top and bottom of the list (chapter 11)

blocks.html: A slide with no material of its own. On top of the project background (solid colour, gradient, image or video) you can place captions, characters, speech bubbles, tickers, badges and stickers. Good for a title screen, chapter breaks, an end card or a conversation-only scene. Click the background in the preview to go to its setting. Set an image later and it becomes an ordinary image slide.
Script on the left opens the script for the current slide. It is also what you see first when you open the editor. The buttons along the top are this slide's lines (script blocks); add one with +.

items.label: Speaker
items.value: The character (or narrator) who says the line. Changing it here leaves the voice as it is

items.label: TTS script
items.value: The text read aloud. Writing hard-to-read words phonetically helps them come out right

items.label: Display captions
items.value: The caption shown on screen. Leave it empty and the TTS script is shown as is. Line breaks split lines; a blank line (two line breaks) starts a new caption page

items.label: Performance
items.value: Adds expressions and pose gestures (chapter 9)

items.label: Buttons
items.value: Copy, play, Record, Import (an audio file) and Delete

blocks.html: Select text in Display captions and buttons such as Emphasis and Add performance appear next to it (chapters 7 and 9).

blocks.text: 🗂️ Script in the header: generate and import

blocks.html: Script in the header opens a screen for making or bringing in the whole script at once.

items.label: Generate
items.value: Pick the audience, style, length, reference URLs, automatic research, reference material, script language, number of speakers, caption lines per page, caption layout, speaking style and TTS method, and generate the script on the spot (needs a Gemini API key)

items.label: Import
items.value: Paste in a script JSON. You can also hand the prompt for external AI, together with your material, to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or similar, and paste back the JSON it returns

items.label: Other ways to import
items.value: Import Audio Bundle ZIP replaces the script, captions and voice of the existing slides all at once

blocks.alt: The Generate screen opened from Script in the header
blocks.caption: Script in the header: Generate

blocks.title: ⚠️ Video slides are skipped
blocks.text: A generated script is filled in, in order, on still-image slides only.

items.label: Voice from a Bundle
items.value: The voice in a finished Bundle ZIP comes in with the import. Audio ZIP in the header also loads an audio Bundle ZIP into the current slide

items.label: Audio files
items.value: Drop MP3, WAV and similar files onto a script block, or pick them with Import

items.label: Microphone
items.value: Record on a script block: record → listen → use it (with trimming at both ends)

items.label: Generate in the app
items.value: With an API key set up, generate per script block, or all at once with Batch voice in the header (chapter 12)

blocks.title: ℹ️ Differences between editions
blocks.text: The Record button does not appear in the Apps Script edition. The local HTML edition is meant to be used without TTS, so the voice-generation features do not appear (recording and importing audio files still work).

sections.intro: From reordering slides to editing the script and generating, importing or recording the voice.

sections.title: Shaping the captions

blocks.html: Captions are set on the Captions tab under Project. It has four sections: Caption design, Name badge, Caption motion and Highlight styles. Where captions sit and how tall the band is are decided by the type on the Screen tab (chapter 11).

blocks.alt: Caption design open on the Captions tab under Project
blocks.caption: Caption design on the Captions tab

items: The designs are arranged in four rows — bands, bands that fit the text, outlines, and shadows and glows — 32 in all
Hover over one to show it in the preview for a moment (nothing changes while “Previewing” shows at the top). Click it to see the list of settings it changes, and Apply to confirm
In a project where characters speak, choose a character under Which caption or bubble to give each character its own design
Size & padding changes the text size and the band padding (narrow, standard, wide)
Adjust design fine-tunes the band shape and colour and the font, colour, outline, shadow and karaoke colour of the text, tab by tab. For the font, Choose from samples lets you hover to compare
You can also use a character's default design (shared by every project) in this project (chapter 9)

blocks.html: Turn on the switch in the heading and the speaking character's name appears at the top left of the caption. Name badge design has tabs for the name, size, position, shape, background and text, and you can drag the badge in the preview.

items: Display animations come in two rows — ones that move the whole caption, and ones that reveal it a character at a time in reading order as it is read — 22 in all. Hover to replay one in the preview
Turn on Karaoke and the text changes colour as it is read. Set the colour under Caption design → Adjust design → Karaoke
In projects with speech bubbles, Different motion for bubbles gives the bubbles their own display animation

blocks.html: Select text in the script's Display captions, press the yellow Emphasis button and pick a style, and just that word changes how it looks. Only the caption's look changes; the reading does not.

items: The look of emphasis is set under Highlight styles on the Captions tab: text colour, font, weight, size, outline, shadow and a marker (colour behind the text). Make as many as you like with + Add style
Customize here… in the list builds a look for just that spot. If you like it, give it a name and Save as preset to add it to the list
The same highlight styles work on sticker, badge and ticker text

blocks.alt: Changing the look of emphasis with Customize here…
blocks.caption: Customize here… (その場で調整…)

blocks.html: Choose a vertical type for the screen and captions and speech bubbles are set vertically. The options switch to vertical ones such as band position (left, centre, right), width and the orientation of Latin letters and digits (9:16 and similar).

sections.intro: How captions look, where they sit, name badges, motion, emphasis and karaoke.

sections.title: Motion and screen transitions

blocks.html: All of these are set for the whole project on the Effects tab under Project. You can also change a single slide or a single boundary.

blocks.alt: Screen transition open on the Effects tab under Project
blocks.caption: The Effects tab

blocks.html: Gives still images a slow zoom or pan. Click Default effect to open the list; hover over one and the current slide plays that motion on a loop. Broadly there are four kinds: zooms, pans, continuous sways (storybook sway, handheld camera, heartbeat and so on) and ones that move only at the start (pop-in, start wide and so on).

items.label: Effect strength
items.value: Subtle / Standard / Strong

items.label: Hide exposed background
items.value: Zooms in slightly, only when the motion would reveal the edges (on by default)

items.label: Auto variety
items.value: Assigns a different motion to each slide in turn

items.label: Change one slide
items.value: This slide → Still image display → Animation. Choosing one here also lets you set its strength, and it takes priority over Project and Auto variety

blocks.title: ℹ️ Not applied to video slides
blocks.text: A video moves by itself, so slide animations are not applied to it. The preview is still while you edit, so try the motion by hovering, or check it with play or Full preview.

blocks.html: How the screen changes the moment one slide moves to the next. New projects use a 0.4-second Fade. Effect type has 21 buttons (three of them have a direction, counted four ways each, for 30 in all); hover over one and the transition from the current slide to the next plays on a loop.

items.label: Transition duration
items.value: Short (0.2 s) / Standard / Long (1 s). Custom: 0.1–3 s

items.label: What changes
items.value: Whole screen (including the background) / slide only (background, characters and captions stay)

items.label: Apply to OP/ED boundaries
items.value: Turn it off and the boundaries with the OP and ED become straight cuts

blocks.html: Click the tag between two slides in the slide list to open Boundary transition and change the type, duration, scope and sound for just that boundary. Boundaries that differ from the project setting have coloured tags. Reset all returns them to the project setting.

items: Transition sound: plays a short sound the moment the slide changes. Seven built-in sounds (storybook page turn, shimmer and so on) or your own sound file. Boundaries that play a sound get a music-note mark on their tag
Text sound without voice: adds a short retro-game-style sound to lines with no voice. Pitch and volume can be set per character

items.label: Before
items.value: From when the slide appears until the speaking starts

items.label: Between lines
items.value: Between one line and the next

items.label: After
items.value: From the end of speaking until the next slide

blocks.html: Short 0.1 s, Standard 0.2 s, Long 0.4 s, or Custom 0–3 s. To change just one gap within a slide, move the voice clip on the timeline (chapter 11).

sections.intro: Slide animations, screen transitions, sound effects and pacing.

sections.title: Characters

blocks.html: Press Create new on the Characters tab under Project. Characters made here are shared across every project and can be picked in any of them (you can also add one in the middle of Start from a use).

blocks.alt: Character editing, with sections for basic settings, character assets, default caption and bubble design, motion and icon appearance
blocks.caption: Editing a character

items.label: Basic settings
items.value: The name (as listed in the script's speaker field). Turn on Narrator (show as captions) to make a character that shows no icon or bubble, only captions

items.label: Character assets
items.value: The artwork and how the mouth moves (the three methods below), plus performance assets (expressions and gestures)

items.label: Default caption and bubble design
items.value: Default caption and Default bubble. Bubble shapes: basic, thought, simple and droplet

items.label: Motion
items.value: Base motion and speaking motion

items.label: Icon appearance
items.value: Crop to a circle / keep the original artwork, and the icon shadow

items.label: Voice settings, set audio adjustment, text sounds
items.value: The voice, speed and pitch applied afterwards, and the text sound for lines with no voice

blocks.html: Save shared character finishes it. Character edits are the one place that waits until you save.

items.label: Registered order
items.html: Registered-order animation: register several still images and they switch in the order you registered them while the character speaks. Two images are enough. Reorder by dragging the cards or with the arrow buttons.

items.label: Animated image
items.html: Single-file animation: register one GIF, animated WebP or APNG file and it plays while the character speaks. The playback speed is adjustable.

blocks.html: 6-image lip sync: six still images switch to follow the loudness of the narration. Each of the six has a fixed role.

items: Eyes open, mouth closed (idle)
Eyes open, mouth half open
Eyes open, mouth open
Eyes closed, mouth closed
Eyes closed, mouth half open
Eyes closed, mouth open

blocks.html: With every method, the character only moves in the video while it is speaking. Assets are kept per method, so switching does not delete them. For voice-driven, Mouth cadence works best on Auto.

A character pack ZIP made in MouthLoop can be added as is, whatever the method. When the app recognises a pack, a confirmation screen shows the expressions and gestures inside. Register character switches the method to voice-driven and brings in the six images plus the performance assets (six expressions and pose gestures) together.

items.label: ZIP file
items.value: up to 50MB

items.label: Number of images
items.value: up to 200

items.label: Total after unpacking
items.value: up to 100MB

items.label: Single-file animation
items.value: up to 12MB / 180 frames (anything larger is scaled down as far as possible, and you are told the resulting size)

items: All at once: under Bulk replace characters at the bottom of the Characters tab, choose From and To and press Run. With Keep existing audio when replacing ticked, the voice stays as it is
Just one line: open the line in Script and choose in the speaker field

items.label: Whole project
items.value: Project → Screen → Adjust layout. Icon size (all), plus size and position (left or right) for each character under Per-character adjustment. Make this the default uses this placement for future projects too

items.label: This slide only
items.value: This slide → Placement → Adjust this slide only. Move or hide the icon and the caption or bubble separately. Copy the same adjustment to other slides

blocks.html: In the preview, drag icons and speech bubbles to move them and use the corners to resize them.

items: Base motion: slow breathing and movement while speaking. None / weak / standard / strong

blocks.html:
🎬 Exporting a video file (MP4, WebM)

Press Export video and the confirmation screen lets you choose the following.

items.label: Export format
items.value: Auto / MP4 / WebM

items.label: Video quality
items.value: Low (4Mbps) / Standard (8Mbps) / High (12Mbps)

blocks.html:
The frame rate can be 30fps (standard) or 60fps (smooth). An estimated file size is shown as well.

🎞️ Export method

At the very top, choose Standard (recording) or High quality (frame rendering). The default, Standard (recording), records while it plays. High quality (frame rendering) waits for each frame to finish before saving it, so dropped frames and audio drift cannot happen even when the computer is busy. It takes longer and needs a supported browser (Chrome, Edge and similar).

blocks.title: ℹ️ Browsers without MP4 support
blocks.text: Some browsers cannot write MP4. In that case the export switches to WebM automatically.

blocks.alt: The video export confirmation: export method, format, quality, frame rate and output resolution
blocks.caption: Confirming a video export

blocks.html: ⚠️ While exporting video

items: Do not close or reload the tab while it is working
Do not switch to another tab, and pause anything heavy
Keep a laptop plugged in and avoid power-saving mode and sleep
Check there is free space where the file will be saved
If you run into trouble, lower the resolution or quality one step and try again
Reload the page after exporting (to free up memory)

blocks.html:
If memory use is high, you are warned before the export starts.

These cautions apply to Standard (recording). High quality (frame rendering) is built so that load cannot drop frames, so other work during the export is fine (keep the page open and do not let the computer sleep).

blocks.title: ⚠️ MP4 compatibility
blocks.text: Even an MP4 export may not upload as is. Some social platforms do not support every codec, so convert to H.264 if you need to.

sections.title: Troubleshooting

items.q: 🧭 I cannot find a setting (I updated from v5.0)
items.a: The layout changed in v5.5. Click what you want to change in the preview and the Adjust this menu takes you to its setting (chapter 5). For one slide only it is This slide; for the whole project it is Project.

items.q: ▶️ Clicking the preview does not play it
items.a: Since v5.5, clicking the preview opens the guide to settings instead of playing. Play with the button in the playback bar under the preview, or the Space key.

items.q: 🔇 No sound, or the preview stops
items.a: Cause: the browser's autoplay blocking is doing its job. Fix: click somewhere inside the page, then play. If that does not help, reload the tab.

items.q: 🐢 Everything is slow, or the export errors out
items.a: Cause: the browser is short on memory (RAM). All video processing happens on your own computer. Fixes: delete projects you no longer need from the dashboard / close spare tabs and pause other work / lower the import quality or the output resolution / restart the browser and try again / always reload the page after an export / split long videos into separate projects and export them individually.

Cause: security software, or clearing “browsing history and cookies” in the browser, erases IndexedDB. Closing a private window does it too. The app cannot recover it. Backing up regularly (ZIP or JSON) is the only defence.

items.q: 🖼️ An animated image will not load
items.a: The file size, frame count, duration or total pixel count may be over the limit. Images likely to exceed a limit are scaled down as far as possible and you are told the resulting size. When a file genuinely cannot load, the message tells you why.

items.q: 🎭 Expressions and gestures are not showing
items.a: Styles that do not display a character image (the band, for example) do not show expressions or gestures. Also check that the assets a performance needs — a MouthLoop character pack — are registered.

items.q: 📊 The runtime and file size shown do not match reality
items.a: The statistics in the header are estimates. They can differ slightly from the file you actually export.

“No API key is set” → enter the key on the Audio tab under Project. “Rate limit” → wait a while and retry (note the free tier's daily ceiling as well). “The API key was rejected” → check you have not entered a Gemini key in the Google Cloud field, and check the key's restrictions. “The Google Cloud API is disabled” → enable the Cloud Text-to-Speech API in the Console.

sections.title: How to update

blocks.html:
If you have already purchased SlideCast Studio, copy the latest version from the same paid note share link you used before.

If you want to carry over your existing projects, library and settings, create a backup first from Backup on the dashboard, just in case.

To update the Apps Script edition while keeping the same URL, replace the files in your existing Apps Script project with the latest versions, then redeploy the existing deployment as a “new version”. Which files to replace depends on the version, so check the update article for that release.

items: Usually two files: 無題.html (“Untitled.html” in the Japanese Apps Script UI) and AppBundle.html
Files starting with “GasAsset_” are sometimes replaced too (three of them in v5.5)
Replace コード.gs (“Code.gs”) as well when the update article says so

blocks.html: If you use the local HTML edition, download “SlideCast Studio〖ローカル版〗.html” — 〖ローカル版〗 means “local edition” — and open it.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Carrying your data over
blocks.text: If you open the app from a new Apps Script project or in a different browser, your earlier data will not appear automatically. Restore it from a backup in that case.
